title: Viniyoga of āpaḥ punantu

words.role: first word of the anuvāka quoted

words.meaning: thus; marks the words before it as a quotation

words.role: with the seer’s name: ‘the seer is …’

words.meaning: anuṣṭubh, the metre of four lines of eight syllables

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (Vedic compound with genitive first member)
words.meaning: Brahmaṇaspati, the lord of the sacred word

words.role: with prāśane: ‘in the sipping of water’
what the mantra is used for

sandhi.rule: a visarga after i becomes r before a voiced consonant

translation.literal: Of the anuvāka “āpaḥ punantu”: the Waters the seer, anuṣṭubh the metre, Brahmaṇaspati the deity, the use in the sipping of water.
translation.readable: Āpaḥ punantu: seer the Waters, metre anuṣṭubh, deity Brahmaṇaspati; used for sipping water.

sandhi_exceptions.note: The prayoga leaves two vowels side by side across a phrase boundary of the formula, without joining them.
The prayoga writes the visarga before the following vowel, the words left apart as separate phrases of the formula, instead of joining them.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: the midday prāśana mantra āpaḥ punantu pṛthivīm (Mahānārāyaṇa 10.30), in the anuṣṭubh metre, whose deity is Brahmaṇaspati, named in the mantra itself. The commas of the witness mark the pauses between the parts; a word before a comma keeps its pausal form.
in_the_rite: Midday service, step prasana, before āpaḥ punantu (M only).
